subtopic_detail: Choosing behavioural therapy ahead of antipsychotic medication for impairing tics
stem:
You are the paediatric registrar seeing an 11 year old boy whose parents are worried about movements that started when he was eight. He blinks hard, jerks his head to the left and shrugs one shoulder, and for the past 18 months he has also cleared his throat repeatedly and made a short barking sound.

He tells you he gets a build up of feeling in his neck beforehand, like an itch he has to scratch, and that he can hold the movements in for a minute or two at the cost of the feeling getting worse until he lets go. The movements settle when he is absorbed in building models and are worst when he is tired or being watched. Between movements he is fully alert with no confusion and no loss of awareness. His handwriting has deteriorated because of the head jerks and two boys have started imitating him in the playground.

data_table.Examination: Multiple motor and vocal tics observed during the consultation, briefly suppressible on request, normal tone, power, coordination and gait
data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, electrolytes, liver function and thyroid stimulating hormone within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate initial management?

options.text: Start clonidine at night and review his tics again in six weeks
options.rationale: An alpha 2 agonist is the preferred medication when attention deficit hyperactivity disorder coexists because it treats both, but there is no attentional complaint here and it still sits behind behavioural therapy (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Arrange an electroencephalogram before any treatment is started
options.rationale: The near pair is myoclonic seizure activity, but seizures are neither preceded by a premonitory urge nor voluntarily suppressible, and awareness is preserved throughout here (Source: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guidelines).
source_refs: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guidelines

options.text: Advise that no treatment is needed and review him in six months
options.rationale: Watchful waiting with psychoeducation is right for tics that do not interfere with function, but his handwriting has deteriorated and he is being teased, which meets the threshold for active treatment (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Refer for a comprehensive behavioural intervention for his tics
options.rationale: Multiple motor tics plus at least one vocal tic persisting beyond a year with a premonitory urge and brief voluntary suppressibility is the characteristic pattern, and behavioural therapy combining habit reversal with function based intervention is first line where it is available, with effect sizes comparable to medication and without metabolic cost (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Start risperidone 0.5 mg at night and review him in four weeks
options.rationale: Antipsychotic treatment reduces tic severity but carries weight gain, sedation and prolactin elevation in a growing child, so it is reserved for tics that remain impairing after a behavioural trial (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Tic disorders are classified by whether tics are motor, vocal or both and by duration, with a year of both types required for the full syndrome. Severity typically peaks between ages 10 and 12 and improves substantially through adolescence in most patients, which is why psychoeducation about the natural history is itself an intervention. Around half of children have coexisting attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and around a third have obsessive compulsive symptoms, and these comorbidities usually cause more functional impairment than the tics themselves. Treatment is driven by impairment rather than by tic count, and school liaison to stop peer imitation and allow discreet release of tics is often as valuable as anything prescribed.
key_points: The premonitory urge with brief voluntary suppressibility distinguishes tics from myoclonus, chorea and seizures.
Behavioural therapy combining habit reversal and function based intervention is first line.
Medication is added when tics remain impairing, chosen according to comorbidity.
Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and obsessive compulsive symptoms usually cause more impairment than the tics.
Severity peaks around ages 10 to 12 and improves through adolescence in most children.
explanation.pearls: Stimulants for coexisting attention deficit hyperactivity disorder were long avoided for fear of worsening tics, but randomised data show tic severity is unchanged or improved, so a stimulant is not contraindicated when the attentional impairment is the greater problem.

subtopic_detail: Requiring prospective symptom charting before treating a suspected premenstrual mood disorder
stem:
You are the general practice registrar seeing a 29 year old woman who says that for five years she has become irritable, tearful and unable to concentrate in the week before her period, and that she once slammed a door hard enough to crack the frame.

She tells you the symptoms lift within two or three days of her period arriving and that she feels entirely herself for the fortnight after that. She has never written any of this down and is describing it from memory. She is not using hormonal contraception and does not wish to conceive in the next year. Her partner has told her the pattern is obvious to him but he has not tracked it either.

data_table.Examination: Reactive affect on the day of review, which is day 8 of her cycle, no psychomotor change and no psychotic features
data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, ferritin, thyroid stimulating hormone and beta human chorionic gonadotrophin within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Start sertraline 50 mg daily and review her again in two cycles
options.rationale: A serotonergic antidepressant is effective once the diagnosis is confirmed, but starting it now removes the untreated baseline that the charting depends on and would treat an underlying disorder inadequately if that is what is present (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Start a combined oral contraceptive and review her in two cycles
options.rationale: Continuous or extended cycle combined contraception is a reasonable second line option after confirmation, but it abolishes the luteal phase and with it any chance of establishing the pattern (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Measure serum progesterone and oestradiol on day 21 of the cycle
options.rationale: Luteal hormone concentrations are normal in this condition, which reflects altered central sensitivity to normal hormonal fluctuation rather than abnormal concentrations, so the test cannot confirm or exclude it (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Refer for gonadotrophin releasing hormone agonist therapy trial
options.rationale: Ovarian suppression is reserved for severe confirmed disease that has failed antidepressant and hormonal treatment, and it requires add back therapy because of bone loss (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Prospective daily symptom rating across two consecutive cycles
options.rationale: The diagnosis requires prospective daily ratings over at least two symptomatic cycles because retrospective accounts are confirmed in only around half of women, the rest turning out to have a premenstrual exacerbation of an underlying mood or anxiety disorder that needs different treatment (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder requires at least five symptoms including one core affective symptom, present in the final week before menses, improving within a few days of onset of menses and minimal in the week after, confirmed by prospective ratings over two symptomatic cycles. The requirement for prospective charting is not bureaucratic: retrospective report agrees with prospective data in only about half of cases, and the alternative explanation, premenstrual exacerbation of an underlying depressive, anxiety or personality disorder, is treated quite differently. Once confirmed, serotonergic antidepressants are first line and can be given continuously or restricted to the luteal phase with similar efficacy, which is unusual among antidepressant indications and reflects a rapid mechanism distinct from the effect in major depression. Second line options include extended cycle combined contraception, and ovarian suppression with add back oestrogen is reserved for refractory disease.
key_points: Two cycles of prospective daily ratings are required before the diagnosis is made.
Retrospective report is confirmed prospectively in only about half of women.
Symptoms must be minimal in the week following menses, which is what separates the disorder from a premenstrual exacerbation.
Luteal hormone concentrations are normal and do not aid diagnosis.
Serotonergic antidepressants work continuously or in the luteal phase alone.
explanation.pearls: The antidepressant effect in this condition appears within a day or two rather than the usual two to four weeks, which is why luteal phase only dosing from ovulation to the onset of bleeding is a legitimate regimen here and nowhere else in psychiatry.

subtopic_detail: Separating a chronic subsyndromal bipolar spectrum illness from affective instability of personality
stem:
You are the psychiatry registrar assessing a 26 year old graphic designer referred with mood swings that have gone on since she was 22. She describes stretches of four or five days at a time when she needs only five hours sleep, works through the night on side projects and talks over people, followed by stretches of a week or so when she is flat, oversleeps and cancels plans.

She has never had a period of elevated mood lasting four full days with the impairment or the number of symptoms her previous psychiatrist described as needed for a formal episode, and she has never been admitted or psychotic. The shifts come on over a day or two and are not obviously set off by arguments or rejections. She has had the same partner for five years and the same three close friends since school, has never self harmed, and does not describe chronic emptiness or fears of abandonment. In four years she has never been free of symptoms for as long as two months.

data_table.Examination: Euthymic on the day of review, normal speech rate, no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation
data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, electrolytes, liver function tests and thyroid stimulating hormone within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Advise watchful waiting with review of her mood in six months
options.rationale: Four years of continuous symptoms with occupational and social consequences is not a watchful waiting problem, and between 15 and 50 per cent of these patients progress to a full bipolar disorder (Source: BMJ Best Practice: Bipolar Disorder).

options.text: Commence a mood stabiliser with psychoeducation and mood charting
options.rationale: Two or more years of alternating subthreshold hypomanic and depressive periods with no symptom free interval beyond two months and no full episode defines a chronic bipolar spectrum illness, and management follows bipolar principles with a mood stabiliser, structured psychoeducation and prospective mood charting (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Commence sertraline 50 mg daily with review again in four weeks
options.rationale: Antidepressant monotherapy in a bipolar spectrum illness risks switching and cycle acceleration, and it is the commonest reason these patients present later with a clear hypomanic episode (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Refer for dialectical behaviour therapy with weekly skills group
options.rationale: The near pair is the affective instability of borderline personality disorder, but there the shifts last hours rather than days, are triggered by interpersonal events, and sit alongside identity disturbance, self harm and chronic emptiness, none of which she describes (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Commence a stimulant trial after formal attention testing is done
options.rationale: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder produces continuous rather than episodic symptoms and begins in childhood, and a stimulant in an unstabilised bipolar spectrum illness can precipitate elevation (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Cyclothymic disorder is defined by at least two years in adults of numerous periods with hypomanic symptoms that never reach episode criteria alternating with depressive symptoms that never reach major episode criteria, present at least half the time and never absent for more than two months. It is chronically under recognised because no single period is dramatic enough to prompt presentation, and patients are frequently labelled as having a personality difficulty instead. The two discriminators that do most work are the duration of a mood shift, days in the bipolar spectrum against hours in borderline personality disorder, and whether shifts are interpersonally triggered. Progression to bipolar I or II is substantial, so treatment follows bipolar principles and antidepressant monotherapy is avoided.
key_points: Two years of alternating subthreshold symptoms with no symptom free interval beyond two months defines the disorder.
Mood shifts lasting days and occurring without interpersonal triggers point away from personality based instability.
Stable relationships, stable identity and absence of self harm argue against borderline personality disorder.
Antidepressant monotherapy risks switching and cycle acceleration.
A substantial minority progress to bipolar I or II disorder over time.
explanation.pearls: Ask what the person was like between the swings: a return to a stable baseline personality between episodes fits the bipolar spectrum, whereas persistent emptiness and identity instability continuing between mood shifts points to a personality disorder even when the swings themselves look similar.

subtopic_detail: Washout interval before a monoamine oxidase inhibitor after a long half life antidepressant
stem:
You are the psychiatry registrar in an outpatient clinic reviewing a 47 year old man with a depressive illness that has not responded to two adequate trials. He completed 12 weeks of sertraline at 200 mg and then eight months of venlafaxine at 225 mg without meaningful improvement.

He was changed to fluoxetine 40 mg daily six months ago and took his last dose three days ago in anticipation of today's appointment. The consultant plans to start moclobemide. He takes no other medication, no over the counter preparations and no herbal products, and he has no cardiac or hepatic disease. His most recent electrolytes and liver function tests were within normal limits.

data_table.Examination: No clonus, no hyperreflexia, no tremor, no diaphoresis, normal tone
data_table.Investigations: Electrolytes, liver function tests and full blood count within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate plan for starting the new agent?

options.text: Start it after a 48 hour gap with close outpatient review
options.rationale: Outpatient monitoring cannot substitute for pharmacokinetic clearance, and serotonin toxicity can progress from tremor and clonus to hyperthermia and rigidity within hours (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Toxicology and Toxinology).

options.text: Cross taper the two agents over the coming fortnight instead
options.rationale: Cross tapering is standard when switching between most antidepressants but is specifically prohibited when a monoamine oxidase inhibitor is one of the pair, because the overlap is the mechanism of toxicity (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

options.text: Wait five weeks after the last fluoxetine dose before starting it
options.rationale: Fluoxetine's active metabolite norfluoxetine has an elimination half life of one to two weeks, so five or more elimination half lives take about five weeks, and this is the interval required before any monoamine oxidase inhibitor is introduced (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Wait two full weeks after the last fluoxetine dose before starting it
options.rationale: Two weeks is the correct washout after most other serotonin reuptake inhibitors, but fluoxetine is the exception because of its metabolite, and applying the general rule here is the classic error (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Start it now because the agent is a reversible inhibitor
options.rationale: Reversibility and selectivity for monoamine oxidase A shorten the washout needed after stopping this agent, not the washout needed before starting it, and serotonin toxicity has been reported with this combination (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic).

explanation.summary: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors remain useful in treatment resistant and atypical depression, but the switching rules around them are the most error prone part of antidepressant prescribing. The general principle is that a washout of five elimination half lives of the parent drug and any active metabolite is required before starting one, and this is two weeks for most reuptake inhibitors but five weeks after fluoxetine. Going in the other direction, two weeks must elapse after stopping an irreversible inhibitor before another serotonergic agent starts, while only 24 hours is needed after the reversible agent moclobemide because enzyme function returns as the drug clears rather than requiring resynthesis. Dietary tyramine restriction is far less onerous with the reversible agent, but interactions with indirect sympathomimetics such as pseudoephedrine remain.
key_points: Washout before a monoamine oxidase inhibitor is five half lives of the drug and its active metabolite.
Fluoxetine requires five weeks; most other reuptake inhibitors require two.
Only 24 hours is needed after stopping moclobemide before a serotonergic agent starts.
Cross tapering is never used when a monoamine oxidase inhibitor is one of the two drugs.
Serotonin toxicity presents with clonus, hyperreflexia, agitation and hyperthermia within hours.
explanation.pearls: Inducible clonus in the lower limbs with agitation or diaphoresis meets the Hunter criteria for serotonin toxicity and is the single most useful bedside sign, because rigidity and hyperthermia appear only once the syndrome is already severe.

subtopic_detail: Distinguishing persistent detachment with intact reality testing from focal seizures and from panic
stem:
You are the psychiatry registrar assessing a 24 year old woman who describes episodes in which she feels as though she is watching herself from a few feet behind her own head, and the room looks flat, like a stage set.

The episodes come on over minutes and last from several hours to most of a day. Throughout them she knows the feeling is not real and can carry on a conversation, drive and work, and afterwards she can recount everything that happened. She has no lip smacking or hand fumbling, no rising sensation in her stomach, no unusual smells and no period of confusion at the end. There is no chest tightness, palpitations or breathlessness with the episodes. They began during a period of daily cannabis use two years ago and have continued unchanged since she stopped 18 months ago.

data_table.Examination: Normal cranial nerve, motor and sensory examination, orientated in time place and person, insight fully preserved
data_table.Investigations: Full blood count, electrolytes, liver function tests, thyroid stimulating hormone and urine drug screen within normal limits

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Arrange magnetic resonance imaging of the brain before treatment
options.rationale: Structural imaging is warranted where the neurological examination is abnormal or where the history suggests focal seizures, and neither applies, so it would delay treatment without changing it (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

options.text: Refer for cognitive behavioural therapy targeting the symptoms
options.rationale: Persistent detachment from self and surroundings with fully intact reality testing, lasting hours and free of autonomic or ictal features, is a dissociative disorder, and psychological therapy addressing catastrophic appraisal of the sensations and safety behaviours such as constant self monitoring is first line (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

options.text: Arrange prolonged video electroencephalogram monitoring first
options.rationale: The near pair is a focal seizure arising from the temporal lobe, which can produce derealisation but lasts one to two minutes rather than hours, impairs awareness or produces automatisms, and is followed by confusion, none of which is present (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

options.text: Start propranolol before predictable stressors and review later
options.rationale: Beta blockade targets the autonomic surge of panic, and she has no palpitations, chest tightness or breathlessness, so the mechanism being treated is not the one operating (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

options.text: Start olanzapine 5 mg at night and review her again in six weeks
options.rationale: Preserved insight that the experience is not real excludes a psychotic disorder, and antipsychotic treatment has no established role and can worsen the subjective sense of detachment (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

explanation.summary: Depersonalisation and derealisation are common transient experiences, reported by up to half the population at some point, and become a disorder only when persistent or recurrent and causing distress or impairment. The defining feature is that reality testing remains intact throughout, which is what separates the condition from psychosis. Onset is frequently precipitated by cannabis, hallucinogens or severe stress, and the symptoms commonly persist long after the substance has been stopped, which patients find frightening and which often drives a fruitless neurological workup. The condition is under diagnosed with an average delay of many years, partly because the experience is hard to describe and patients fear being thought psychotic.
key_points: Intact reality testing throughout is what separates the disorder from psychosis.
Duration of hours to days separates it from focal seizures, which last one to two minutes.
Absence of an autonomic surge separates it from panic attacks.
Cannabis and hallucinogens are frequent precipitants and symptoms outlast cessation.
Psychological therapy is first line; no medication has established efficacy.
explanation.pearls: Comorbid depression or anxiety is present in most cases and treating it often reduces the dissociative symptoms substantially, so screening for and treating the comorbidity does more than any agent aimed at the detachment itself.
